sections.title: What are Large Language Models?
sections.body: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are advanced computer programs that understand and generate human language. They are built using a type of artificial intelligence called neural networks, specifically designed to learn from vast amounts of text data.

sections.title: How Do LLMs Process Text?
sections.body: LLMs break down text into smaller pieces called tokens, which can be words or parts of words. These tokens are then transformed into numerical representations, known as embeddings, that help the model understand the meaning and relationships between different words.

sections.title: The Role of Prompts
sections.body: Prompts are the questions or instructions we give to LLMs to guide their responses. Even small changes in these prompts can lead to very different answers, making prompt design an important skill for getting the best results from LLMs.

sections.title: Improving LLM Performance
sections.body: Techniques like prompt engineering and automatic prompt generation help customize how LLMs respond. By structuring prompts effectively, we can enhance the accuracy and relevance of the answers, especially for complex tasks that require step-by-step reasoning.

sections.title: Challenges with LLMs
sections.body: Despite their capabilities, LLMs can sometimes produce incorrect or misleading information, known as hallucinations. This is why careful prompt design is crucial, especially in educational settings where reliable answers are essential.
